rgb: This is a confined indoor locker room, with grey metal lockers lining the left wall and a blue doorway roughly 4 to 5 metres ahead in the background. A person wearing a grey 'BANGKOK' hoodie and blue surgical mask stands immediately ahead and a little right of the camera wearer, within arm's reach at approximately 0.4 to 0.6 metres, holding a smartphone with both hands at chest height. During the first three frames, the foreground person faces at an angle toward the left and looks down at the phone, while the top half of their head is cut off by the upper frame boundary. In frame 4, they rotate their torso and masked face to point more directly toward the camera wearer, then turn slightly left again in frame 5, when a different hand enters from the lower-right edge and touches their left upper arm. Behind the hoodie wearer on the left, someone in a white 'JAMES 10' jersey begins about 1.2 metres away with their back to the camera, then moves farther down the left-hand lockers to around 2.5 to 3 metres away and leans forward over a bench from frames 3 through 5. Several more people dressed in dark shirts and tank tops remain in the background corridor at distances of 2 to 4.5 metres, partly blocked by the hoodie wearer and the white-jersey person. In frame 3, a person in a black t-shirt briefly advances into the central opening to about 1.5 metres away while facing the camera wearer, but is hidden by the hoodie wearer in frame 4.
depth: The depth visualization depicts a tight locker-room space with a masked person in a 'BANGKOK' hoodie positioned on the right within arm's reach, about 0.4–0.6 m from the camera wearer. They hold a smartphone at chest-to-waist height, roughly 0.3–0.5 m ahead of and slightly below the camera. On the left, 0.5–1.5 m behind this foreground person, someone wearing a white 'JAMES 10' jersey bends forward with their back turned toward the camera and faces a row of lockers at the far left; in frames 3–5, those lockers extend into the foreground at 0.3–0.6 m. Two to three other people occupy the corridor farther behind at approximately 1.5–4.0 m. Throughout all five frames, the foreground person remains reachable by arm and rotates their torso somewhat toward the camera in frame 4. In frame 5, the camera wearer's own hand reaches onto their left arm. Meanwhile, as the camera moves left beside the lockers, the 'JAMES 10' wearer withdraws from about 1.0 m away in frame 1 to 1.8 m away in frames 3–5. The map distinctly separates the foreground person's outstretched hands and phone from both their torso and the slanted locker wall, providing a continuous distance gradient that is more difficult to assess from RGB alone. It also shows the cropping of the person's upper head and lower body and their partial blockage of people behind them. Depth becomes unreliable past 2 m, however, because the distant people, blue door, and corridor walls blend into an almost uniformly black region. It is also unreliable in frame 3, where the foreground person's left shoulder and neck are excessively saturated to the same brightness as the nearer left hand.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation view separates the people and handheld object inside the locker room. It repeatedly identifies the foreground person on the right at 0.4–0.6 m, oriented leftward and somewhat toward the camera while watching their phone instead of the camera wearer; everything above their nose and below their hips lies outside the image. In frames 1–2, the map distinguishes the white-jersey person on the left, who is 1.0–1.5 m away, facing away, and bending downward, along with two to three people standing another 0.5–1.5 m behind that person. Those background individuals are 2.0–3.5 m from the camera and face variously toward or away from it. By frames 4–5, the lockers and foreground person conceal most of this background group. The smartphone held within arm's reach of both the foreground person and the camera wearer sits 0.3–0.5 m away, to the left of the foreground torso and below head height. It moves slightly downward in frame 4 and rises in frame 5 while another hand touches the foreground person's right-side sleeve. Relative to RGB, the masks make separate, overlapping people easier to count in frame 2's dim background, although fixed structural features such as the close lockers on the left and faraway walls are omitted entirely. Several outputs are unreliable: the phone is completely absent in frames 1, 4, and 5; in frame 2, it is labeled both as a 'bottle' and an overlapping 'cell phone'; in frame 3, the bent 'JAMES 10' torso is incorrectly identified as a 'backpack'; and that person disappears entirely in frames 4–5. The system also joins the foreground person's hands with either the phone or torso.
pose: Displayed against a black background, the body-and-hand skeleton visualization follows joint positions and primarily captures the foreground person's left hand from the lower-left through center-left area. That hand is 0.3–0.5 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach of both the foreground person and the wearer, and holds and taps the smartphone in every one of the five frames. Over the sequence, the magenta hand skeleton travels from the lower left in frame 1 into the centre during frames 2–3, falls to the bottom border in frame 4 as the arms descend, and reappears in the lower centre in frame 5. A second magenta hand skeleton then appears at the lower right, about 0.3 m from the first, where a hand reaches onto the foreground person's arm. Frame 3 also contains a yellow upper-body rectangle and head landmarks in the upper-left quadrant for the white-jersey person, positioned about 1.5–1.8 m away and 1.0 m behind the foreground hands. These marks capture that person's forward-leaning, downward-facing posture directed away from the camera wearer. The map exposes precise finger positioning and hand direction, including fingers spread above the screen in frames 2–3 and fingers gripping the sleeve in frame 5, even where RGB motion blur and skin-to-skin contact obscure the joint locations. Overall, however, pose detection is very unreliable: across every frame it entirely misses the foreground person's head, torso, and right hand, probably because of severe close-distance cropping and occlusion; it detects none of the background people in frames 1, 2, or 4; and in frame 5 it fabricates a warped yellow body skeleton tangled among the foreground hands.
